account:
Today I am following my appointments, though the ten o'clock mill grain inspection is still pending. I have counted eighty-eight hay bales and eighty emeralds in the mill stall chest and read the posted price of two emeralds per bale. That establishes the visible stock, not grain quality or the state of deliveries; neither the secretary nor I has yet identified the grain custodian. My next scheduled engagements are lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at fifteen, and the office at sixteen-thirty.

Something unusual is the repeated, identical fragment 'bridge or port change at bakery.' I have heard it from several townspeople, including Townsfolk 01 and 21 near the mill, but have no original source or concrete description of a change. Freight reportedly described ordinary deliveries and warehouse work; the neighbour said freight was busy and that the baker wanted bread for a gathering arranged beforehand. Those reports might concern ordinary preparations, but do not resolve the rumour.

The innkeeper has been seen carrying a sack of bread and has repeatedly asked about an eighteen o'clock great hall inspection. The secretary told the innkeeper that I approved it and would meet the builder at the hall entrance at seventeen fifty-five. The innkeeper also invited me directly, saying the hall would be ready. My retained notes do not independently establish that approval, although they may omit earlier discussion. The hall preparations, bread arrangements, and builder meeting suggest an organized gathering or event. They might be connected, but I have not seen proof of its purpose or of any connection to the bridge-or-port talk. I should clarify the added appointment and ask directly what is being prepared rather than treat repetition or secrecy as evidence of wrongdoing.
